title: Local term of a correspondence
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] (so $k$ is an algebraic
closure of $k_0$) and the coefficient
conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], writing
$E_{\mathrm{coeff}}/\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the finite coefficient field
and $A=A_{E_{\mathrm{coeff}},n}$ for its finite coefficient ring
($n\geq1$), to distinguish the coefficient field from the scheme $E$ below. Put $s=\Spec k$, and let $E$ be a separated finite-type
$s$-scheme, using the morphism conventions of
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Throughout, the structure morphisms of $E$ and of the
open-and-closed subschemes of $E$ considered below are assumed
exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility], so
that their dualizing complexes of [def-trf-dualizing-complex] are
defined.

*Restricted sections.* Let $\sigma:A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$ be a section
(a morphism in $D(E,A)$), and let $j_B:B\hookrightarrow E$ be the
inclusion of an open-and-closed subscheme: $B$ is the open subscheme
on a subset of $E$ that is both open and closed
[def-weil-open-immersion]. The *restriction* of
$\sigma$ to $B$ is

$$
j_B^*\sigma:\;
A_B\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Lj_B^*A_E
\xrightarrow{Lj_B^*\sigma}
Lj_B^*\omega_{E,A}
\longrightarrow\omega_{B,A},
$$

the first arrow being the inverse of the constant-coefficient pullback
isomorphism (the exact pullback and constant-ring identification of
[prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact,
prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], with derived pullback as in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]), and the last arrow being the
canonical identification
$Lj_B^*\omega_{E,A}\cong Rj_B^!\omega_{E,A}\cong\omega_{B,A}$
obtained from the equality $Rj_B^!\cong Lj_B^*$ for the open immersion
$j_B$ (the purity clause of the six-operations package
[prop-functor-package], item (6), in relative dimension $0$) and the
composition isomorphism of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]
applied to $j_B$. This restricted section is defined for every
open-and-closed $B$, whether or not $B$ (or $E$) is proper over $s$.

*Local terms.* If moreover $B$ is proper over $s$, the *local term*
of $\sigma$ on $B$ is

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(\sigma):=\int_B j_B^*\sigma\in A,
$$

the integral of [def-trf-integration]; properness of $B$ is needed
only for this scalar integral, and the ambient $E$ need not be proper.

*Endocorrespondences.* Let $c$ be an admissible correspondence in the
sense of [def-trf-correspondence], with
$u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ and fixed scheme
$F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$ be its trace class of
[def-trf-trace-class]. For an open-and-closed $B\subseteq F$, proper
over $s$, put

$$
\operatorname{LT}_B(u):=\operatorname{LT}_B\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\bigr)
=\int_B j_B^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\in A;
$$

$F$ itself need not be proper. In particular, when $F$ is proper over
$s$ and has finitely many open-and-closed components
$\beta\in\pi_0(F)$ in the sense of [def-trf-fixed-scheme], each $\beta$
is open-and-closed in $F$ and proper over $s$
[lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and we write

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta:=j_\beta^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u):
A_\beta\longrightarrow\omega_{\beta,A},
\qquad
\operatorname{LT}_\beta(u):=
\int_\beta\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)|_\beta\bigr)\in A
$$

for the *local term* of $u$ at $\beta$.

*Point components.* If $\bar x$ is a point of $F$ such that $\{\bar x\}$
is open and closed in $F$ and the open-and-closed subscheme $B_{\bar x}\subseteq F$
with underlying set $\{\bar x\}$ is reduced
[def-pc-reduced-scheme], then it is a nonempty reduced irreducible scheme,
hence integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and has dimension $0$
[def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus its structure morphism is an
isomorphism $B_{\bar x}\simeq\Spec k$ by
[lem-weil-pbc-zero-dim-integral-point] ($k$ is algebraically closed and
$B_{\bar x}$ is of finite type over $k$), so $B_{\bar x}$ is proper over
$s$, and we write
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar x}(u):=\operatorname{LT}_{B_{\bar x}}(u)$,
the local term on the reduced open-and-closed point component of
$\bar x$. This applies to every Frobenius fixed point: for the
Frobenius correspondence $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$,
with $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, in the admissible setting above, on
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, with $X_0$ of finite type over $k_0$ and $\Phi$
the $k$-linear base change of the $q$-power scheme Frobenius of $X_0$
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius], the fixed scheme is the disjoint union of reduced points $\Spec k$, one for each
$y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$, by [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], and
$\operatorname{LT}_{\bar y}(u)=\operatorname{LT}_y(u)$ denotes the local
term on the component indexed by $y$.

split_report.summary: Audited the construction against both blueprint snapshots and every cited statement. Kept restriction for arbitrary ambient E and integration only on proper clopen B, explicitly named the coefficient, morphism, constant-pullback, reducedness and point-geometry interfaces, and reused the existing closed-immersion properness and zero-dimensional integral-point results rather than adding nodes. Made the positive Frobenius exponent and the preceding admissible correspondence context explicit, without adding a separate hypothesis on X_0. The existing Lean localTerm assumes ambient properness and does not attach. This is a definition: proof and proof_deps remain empty. Second reading distinguishes the coefficient field E_coeff from the ambient scheme E and specifies the k-linear base-changed scheme Frobenius, citing its existing definition. Maintainer reading: the point-component hypothesis now says that the singleton is open and closed in F, as the source's open-and-closed subscheme B_x and every citer already presuppose; previously closedness was used without citation (it holds for the finite-type F by the Jacobson property, so no case is lost).
split_report.blueprint: Realizes Restricted sections, Local terms, Endocorrespondences and Point components of def-trf-local-term in main-20261015 (same construction as master). No proof route or unit realization is changed; this node is not the supported-pairing unit key node.
